newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Gunmen raid restaurant owned by Sri Lankan MP.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen raid restaurant owned by Sri Lankan MP.

text.p: Gunmen attacked and robbed a restaurant owned by an opposition member of parliament in downtown Colombo, witnesses and police said on Sunday.

About 20 gunmen burst into the Chinese restaurant on Saturday night, sprayed it with bullets and stole cash from the register, Sarath Kongahage, the owner and a member of the main opposition United National Party (UNP), said.
No one was hurt but some of the diners were also robbed by the attackers, Kongahage told Reuters.
"We were having dinner when we heard shouts, the sound of breaking glass, then men ran into the room with rifles and sprayed the place with bullets," he said.
"They smashed the place up and looted some money," he said, adding that he escaped by jumping out of the window.
The attackers had come in three trucks, Kongahage said.

Police said it was not clear if the raid was linked to continuing unrest after last week's killing of a ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition lawmaker, Nalanda Ellawala, who was cremated on Saturday.
On Saturday police fired teargas and called in support from the army after some of the estimated 100,000 mourners set fire to shops and threw stones at the police station during Ellawala's cremation.
